item.text:
**8B.2 Research Note: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in 2024**

**Synthesis**
The record shows Erdoğan translating parts of his program into concrete machinery: a named annual program, a heavily budgeted investment program, technocratic central-bank staffing, sectoral public procurement systems, and IMF/FATF-endorsed macro and AML/CFT reforms. The weaker side is enforcement: accountability for local officials, opposition-held municipalities, and information controls remained selective, opaque, and coercive rather than rule-bound.

This is concrete evidence of a program broken into operational policy lanes. | 8B.2 |

This is a direct negative example of weak enforcement and blocked accountability. | 8B.2, 7B.10 |

This is strong evidence of selective institutional control. | 8B.2, 8B.1, 7B.10 |

This is concrete enforcement of information control, not transparent program execution. | 8B.2, 7B.10 |
| Freedom in the World 2024: Turkey | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says officials were widely accused of publishing distorted data, state media favored the AKP, and key appointments after 2023 improved transparency only in some areas. This is mixed evidence: some policy translation improved credibility, but broader enforcement still leaned toward regime protection and message control. | 8B.2, 7B.10 |

**Search gap**
I did not find a single authoritative 2024 presidential document that cleanly bundles priorities, budgets, appointments, timelines, and enforcement into one unified Erdoğan program. Instead, the implementation trail is distributed across the annual program, the investment program, central-bank staffing, IMF/World Bank planning, procurement systems, and coercive enforcement cases.
